newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil close to deciding on higher CS sugar quota.
newsitem.headline: Brazil close to deciding on higher CS sugar quota.

text.p: The Brazilian government is close to a decision on whether to increase authorizations for sugar exports from the center-south based on evaluations of the size of the region's crop, a top government sugar official said.

While the private sector is hoping for an extra 500,000 tonnes, the actual amount will depend on evaluations of the size of the crop and alcohol stocks, said the head of the sugar and alcohol department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.
"The actual figure is not clear yet but it will be around 500,000 tonnes or below," said Pedro Cabral.
Under a government crop plan published in June, the country's center-south crop, harvested traditionally between May and November, was forecast at 10.47 million tonnes.
But now the harvest is expected to be higher, Cabral said.
"We are working on the numbers at the moment but it will be bigger," Cabral said.

As of December 1, sugar production in the center-south was already 10.17 million tonnes against 8.98 million by the same stage last year, according to figures from the Sugar and Alcohol Industries Association in Sao Paulo (AIAA).
Within the crop plan, the region's export quota was previously set at 3.68 million tonnes, with 6.80 million tonnes expected to be consumed internally.

As of end-November, sugar shipments from Brazil's key ports in the center-south had reached 3.48 million tonnes since the start of the crop year in May, virtually unchanged from last year, according to port authority statistics.

Cabral said a decision on the quota increase would be reached after the Finance and Industry and Commerce ministers returned from a Mercosul summit in the northern city of Fortaleza being held this week.
"Without doubt, there will be a decision before Christmas," Cabral said.
For the time being, there was no question of increasing the export quota for the north/northeast producing region where the harvest runs from September to April.
"It is too early to talk about that," Cabral said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
